arxiv-2011-00936.title: Distributing bipartite quantum systems under timing constraints
arxiv-2011-00936.creator: Kianna Wan
arxiv-2011-00936.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Kianna Wan. In many quantum information processing protocols, entangled states shared among parties are an important resource. In this article, we study how bipartite states may be distributed in the context of a quantum network limited by timing constraints. We explore various tasks that plausibly arise in this context, and characterize the achievability of several of these in settings where only one-way communication is allowed. We provide partial results in the case where two-way communication is allowed.

arxiv-2103-09207.title: The role of vimentin-nuclear interactions in persistent cell motility through confined spaces
arxiv-2103-09207.creator: Sarthak Gupta 1 , Alison E. Patteson 1 , J. M. Schwarz 1,2
arxiv-2103-09207.description: Abstract The ability of cells to move through small spaces depends on the mechanical properties of the cellular cytoskeleton and on nuclear deformability. In mammalian cells, the cytoskeleton is composed of three interacting, semi-flexible polymer networks: actin, microtubules, and intermediate filaments (IF).

arxiv-2110-06578.title: Nonlinearity-induced transition in nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model and nonlinear higher-order topological system
arxiv-2110-06578.creator: Motohiko Ezawa
arxiv-2110-06578.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Motohiko Ezawa. We study the topological physics in nonlinear Schrödinger systems on lattices. We employ the quench dynamics to explore the phase diagram, where a pulse is given to a lattice point and we analyze its time evolution. There are two system parameters λ \lambda and ξ \xi , where λ \lambda controls the hoppings between the neighboring links and ξ \xi controls the nonlinearity. The dynamics crucially depends on these system parameters.

arxiv-2307-08769.title: The impact of electric currents on Majorana dark matter at freeze out
arxiv-2307-08769.creator: Lukas Karoly, David C. Latimer
arxiv-2307-08769.description: Abstract Thermal relics with masses in the GeV to TeV range remain possible candidates for the Universe’s dark matter (DM). These neutral particles are often assumed to have vanishing electric and magnetic dipole moments so that they do not interact with single real photons, but the anapole moment can still be nonzero, permitting interactions with single virtual photons.

arxiv-2309-07469.title: Floquet edge solitons in modulated trimer waveguide arrays
arxiv-2309-07469.creator: Shuang Shen (沈双), Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Yongdong Li (李永东), Yiqi Zhang (张贻齐)
arxiv-2309-07469.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shuang Shen (沈双), Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Yongdong Li (李永东), Yiqi Zhang (张贻齐). We show that one-dimensional Floquet trimer arrays with periodically oscillating waveguides support two different and co-existing types of topological Floquet edge states in two different topological gaps in Floquet spectrum.

arxiv-2312-04907.title: New 511 keV line data provides strongest sub-GeV dark matter constraints
arxiv-2312-04907.creator: Pedro De la Torre Luque, Shyam Balaji, Joseph Silk
arxiv-2312-04907.description: Abstract We explore the 511 511 keV emission associated to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles that can produce electron-positron pairs and form positronium after thermalizing. We use ∼ 16 \sim 16 yr of SPI data from INTEGRAL to constrain DM properties, including the full positron propagation and losses, and the free electron density suppression away from the Galactic plane.

arxiv-2404-07184.title: Homology of Moment Frames
arxiv-2404-07184.description: Abstract Using homological techniques we show that a pin-anchored frame that involves only moments and shears provides a conceptual bridge between the statics of moment frames and the kinematics of pin-jointed trusses. One immediate result is a long exact sequence whose alternating sum of dimensions gives a novel counting rule for self-stresses and mechanisms.

arxiv-2502-18132.title: A kinetic model of solar wind acceleration driven by ambipolar electric potential and velocity-space diffusion
arxiv-2502-18132.creator: M. Péters de Bonhome, V. Pierrard, F. Bacchini
arxiv-2502-18132.description: Abstract Context. Parker Solar Probe (PSP) observations have revealed that most of the solar wind acceleration occurs very close to the Sun. This acceleration is partly due to the global electric potential originating from the mass disparity between electrons and protons, coupled with the constraints of charge quasi-neutrality and zero-current conditions in the solar wind plasma.

arxiv-2511-05149.title: Improving Injection-Throttling Mechanisms for Congestion Control for Data-center and Supercomputer Interconnects
arxiv-2511-05149.creator: Cristina Olmedilla, Jesus Escudero-Sahuquillo, Pedro J. Garcia, Francisco J. Quiles, Jose Duato
arxiv-2511-05149.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cristina Olmedilla, Jesus Escudero-Sahuquillo, Pedro J. Garcia, Francisco J. Quiles, Jose Duato. Over the past decade, Supercomputers and Data centers have evolved dramatically to cope with the increasing performance requirements of applications and services, such as scientific computing, generative AI, social networks or cloud services. This evolution have led these systems to incorporate high-speed networks using faster links, end nodes using multiple and dedicated accelerators, or a advancements in memory technologies to bridge the memory bottleneck.

europmc-pmc7278864.description: The Covid-19 pandemic led to lockdowns in several parts of the world and, hence, changed some daily habits, including social interactions, the ability to perform sports, and-possibly-diet. The Italian government established and promulgated lockdown policies on 9 March 2020. We...

pmc-11046991.title: Opportunistic optimisation of inhaler technique in hospitalised adults with asthma: a two-phase quality improvement project
pmc-11046991.creator: Mrinalini Dey, Koushan Kouranloo, Joseph Hanna, Ananya Singh, Alice Rafferty, Stephen Scott
pmc-11046991.description: inhaler technique. We undertook a quality improvement project to opportunistically optimise inhaler technique in adults with asthma. We aimed to investigate effectiveness of two different educational methods to improve inhaler technique in patients diagnosed with asthma, hospitalised with a non-asthma-related diagnosis. Materials and methods We undertook a real-world, opportunistic quality improvement project.

pmc-11432347.title: Silent Threats of the Heart: A Case Series and Narrative Review on Suicide Left Ventricle Post-Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients with Dynamic LVOT Obstruction and Aortic Stenosis
pmc-11432347.creator: Silvia Romano, Emilio D’Andrea, Dan Alexandru Cozac, Maria Teresa Savo, Antonella Cecchetto, Anna Baritussio, Marika Martini, Massimo Napodano, Barbara Bauce, Valeria Pergola
pmc-11432347.description: Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in Europe and North America, with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) revolutionizing its management. Hypertrophic left ventricle (HLV) frequently coexists with AS, complicating treatment due to the associated risk of left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, heart failure, and sudden death.

pmc-11445099.title: OTHR-11 A CASE SERIES OF OUTER TABLE CALVARIAL DECORTICATION AS A VIABLE OPTION TO ACHIEVE SKULL COVER AFTER RESECTION OF LARGE SCALP TUMORS
pmc-11445099.creator: Daniel Dzinotyiwei, Kazadi Kalangu, Nathaniel Zimani, Maximilian Dzowa
pmc-11445099.description: A showcase of a scalp cover technique that offers a simple solution to a unique challenge posed by excision of late presenting large scalp tumors in a third-world setting through a case series of 2 patients with extensive scalp malignancy requiring wide local excision with striping of the pericranium.

pmc-12365046.title: Digital divides in telehealth accessibility for cancer care in the United States
pmc-12365046.creator: Lingbo Liu, Tracy Onega, Erika L Moen, Anna N A Tosteson, Rebecca E Smith, Qianfei Wang, Lauren Cowan, Fahui Wang
pmc-12365046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Telehealth has been promoted as a solution to spatial healthcare access barriers, yet its role in addressing cancer care disparities remains uncertain, particularly in the context of digital divides in broadband availability and affordability. This study assessed spatial and telehealth accessibility to cancer care across 33,499 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTA) in the United States using the two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) and two-step virtual catchment area (2SVCA) methods, respectively.

pmc-12468475.title: Skeletal Maturity Assessment in Pediatric ACL-Reconstruction
pmc-12468475.creator: Umile Giuseppe Longo, Mariajose Villa Corta, Federica Valente, Laura Ruzzini, Pieter D’hooghe, Kristian Samuelsson, Frank A Cordasco, Alexander S Nicholls, James T Bennett
pmc-12468475.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Skeletal maturity significantly influences surgical decision-making and outcomes in pediatric ACL reconstruction.A multimodal approach combining clinical, radiological, and MRI-based assessments enhances accuracy in determining skeletal maturity. What are the implications of the main findings? Tailoring ACL reconstruction techniques to skeletal maturity levels minimizes growth disturbances and improves functional outcomes.

pmc-12612177.title: SPEED-TR: a self-distilled and pre-trained transformer model for enhanced ECG detection of tricuspid regurgitation
pmc-12612177.creator: Xiaolin Diao, Wei Xu, Huaibing Cheng, Ya Zhou, Yang Liu, Yanni Huo, Jianli Lu, Jinghan Huang, Jia He, Fang Liu, Zhihui Cao, Xue Zhang, Wei Zhao, Xiaohan Fan
pmc-12612177.description: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remains underdiagnosed due to the lack of effective screening tools. We developed a self-distilled and pre-trained transformer model for detecting TR (SPEED-TR) from electrocardiography. The model was trained using 466,149 electrocardiogram-echocardiogram pairs from 291,673 patients and validated in one internal (63,925 patients) and two external cohorts (44,951 and 21,300 patients).

pmc-12638137.title: Detrimental Synergistic Effects of Atmospheric Ozone and Polystyrene Nanoparticle Exposure on Human Adult Myogenic Progenitor Cells
pmc-12638137.creator: Cristina Purcaro, Ester Sara Di Filippo, Cecilia Paolini, Piero Di Carlo, Stefania Fulle
pmc-12638137.description: Ozone (O3) and polystyrene nanoparticles (PNPs) display diffusive behavior that leads to toxicity in many tissues of the adult organism. In this study, we evaluated the interactions between atmospheric pollutants and human muscle, using human myogenic progenitor cells (huMPCs) derived from vastus lateralis skeletal muscle.

pmc-13137114.title: Efficiency and Safety of Endoscopic Injection Sclerotherapy With Ligation for Esophageal Varices: A Retrospective Study.
pmc-13137114.creator: Keita Maki, Hiroaki Haga, Kyoko Hoshikawa, Tomohiro Katsumi, Fumiya Suzuki, Fumi Uchiyama, Yoshiyuki Ueno
pmc-13137114.description: ObjectivesEndoscopic injection sclerotherapy with ligation (EISL) is a combined endoscopic treatment that involves endoscopic injection sclerotherapy (EIS) and endoscopic variceal ligation. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of conventional EIS and EISL in treating esophageal varices and the usefulness of EISL.

pmc-13161669.description: Variants in the Glucokinase Regulator (GCKR) gene are increasingly being detected with growing applications of genomic sequencing technologies. Despite the crucial roles of the GCKR gene in energy homeostasis, the clinical applications of GCKR variants are currently limited. pmc-13649510.title: Artificial intelligence in hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis and AI-assisted treatment support: Current landscape and future directions
pmc-13649510.creator: Quan-Kai Lei, Tong-Xv Wu, Chu-Long Zhang, Yun-Wen Zheng
pmc-13649510.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains challenging to diagnose and manage, particularly at an early stage when curative treatment is most feasible. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers tools for integrating histopathology, radiology, laboratory testing, demographics, and electronic health records, while also creating opportunities for clinician-supervised AI-assisted procedural support.
